results.title: Russia prepares for possible jet fuel sanctions via state reserves
results.description: Russian Energy Minister Alexander Novak stated that jet fuel reserves established under the national energy security program are sufficient to maintain normal flight operations for several months, even if new sanctions restrict supplies to Russian airlines. The reserves and the ability of domestic refineries to scale output form the basis of the ministry's assessment. No sanctions targeting Russian carriers have been enacted to date. The prospective risk is linked by officials to international security operations in the Middle East. Airlines say they are preparing for multiple scenarios. Reserve and production basis Novak said the reserves were created specifically within the framework of the country's energy security program. He added that Russian refineries possess the technical capacity to increase jet fuel production volumes if external restrictions materialize.
